feedback.details: Diagram passes mmdc validation (exit 0) and correctly uses `flowchart LR` per critic system rules (C4Container/C4Boundary are banned by the critic system). However, non-standard Mermaid node shapes are used: cylinder `[("...")]` for User (line 337) and PostgreSQL (line 344), queue shape `[["..."]]` for Telegram (line 338) and Pinecone (line 339). The sprint contract says 'must strictly use C4 container syntax extensions' which conflicts with critic rules banning C4 syntax — the flowchart approach is correct per critic system, but exotic node shapes reduce clarity.

The contract requires 'exactly these containers: User, API Gateway, Database, Knowledge Base Vector Store.' The diagram contains 5 nodes (lines 337-344): User, Telegram, Pinecone, API Gateway, PostgreSQL. Telegram is an extra node beyond the 4 required. Diagram node labels lack 'Description' fields — only minimal tech annotations exist. Full descriptions are in the narrative (lines 24-62) but not in the diagram. Relationships use descriptive verbs ('Executes SQL queries') rather than standard C4 types ('Uses', 'Reads', 'Writes'). PostgreSQL and User use cylinder shapes which is semantically incorrect for a person/container.

CRITICAL: Zero H1 headings exist in the document (confirmed by grep). The contract mandates 'H1 Title' as mandatory. The file starts directly with `## H2 Scope` (line 5). All headings literally contain 'H2'/'H3' in their text (e.g., '## H2 Scope', '## H3 Component Details'), which is non-standard. Technical terms 'ACID' (line 17), 'JWT' (line 33), 'libpq' (line 17), 'WAL' (line 124) are used without definition on first use. Passive voice usage is ~3%, well under 15%. No prohibited adjectives found.

Table (lines 66-135) maps FR6-FR55 and NFR1-NFR17 comprehensively. Contract specifies 'DB-001, KB-002' format IDs but document uses raw FR/NFR IDs — this was flagged in Rounds 1-4 and remains unresolved. Deferred requirements table (lines 137-160) provides risk levels and mitigation strategies. Functional requirements coverage is 100% with Deferred items having justification. No formal 'Deferred' subsection heading exists.

Excellent coverage. (1) Database connection string (lines 166-175): format, example, ENV variable, pool configuration. (2) KB API schemas (lines 180-245): Vector Upsert and Query with full JSON bodies, headers, success/error responses. (3) Authentication (lines 247-262): PostgreSQL SCRAM-SHA-256, Pinecone Bearer token, API Gateway JWT with token lifecycle. All copy-pasteable and specific.

Multiple violations: (1) Missing H1 heading — zero `# ` headings exist. (2) Code blocks without language labels at lines 165, 180, 213 — bare ``` fences. (3) Missing closing quote on line 313: `**Mitigation Strategy':`. (4) Typo 'load balenger' on line 303. (5) Heading text literally contains 'H2'/'H3' prefixes. No trailing whitespace detected. Blank lines around headings present. File ends with newline.

All four failure modes documented comprehensively (lines 264-328): (1) DB Connection Pool Exhaustion with pool config, fallback HTTP 429, Redis queue, metrics. (2) KB Vector Index Corruption with daily checks, snapshots, PostgreSQL fallback, metrics. (3) Schema Migration Rollback with Flyway, blue-green deployment, automatic rollback, metrics. (4) High Latency Fallback with L1/L2 cache, stale-while-revalidate, single-flight pattern, metrics. Each has mitigation, fallback, monitoring metric, and alert channel.

overall_summary: The database/c2-container.md shows measurable improvement from prior Sprint 5 rounds but has two persistent critical failures blocking contract approval. (1) The document is missing its H1 root heading entirely — the contract mandates 'H1 Title' but the file starts at H2 with literal 'H2' text prefixes in heading labels, a formatting antipattern persisting across multiple rounds. (2) Code blocks lack language labels (lines 165, 180, 213 — bare ``` fences). The PRD Traceability Matrix still uses raw FR/NFR IDs instead of the contract-specified DB-001/KB-002 format despite being flagged in Rounds 1-4. The diagram correctly places Pinecone outside the system subgraph (fixing the recurring antipattern from Rounds 3-4), but includes Telegram as a 5th node beyond the 4 required containers and uses semantically incorrect cylinder shapes for User/PostgreSQL. Interface Contract Documentation (9.5) and Adversarial Edge Case Coverage (9.5) are the strongest areas — both provide exhaustive, copy-pasteable specifications. Typos remain: 'load balenger' (line 303) and missing closing quote (line 313).
